enzyme_name: Glutathione-cystine transhydrogenase (thiol-disulfide oxidoreductase; glutaredoxin/thioltransferase class, EC 1.8.4.4)
organism_context: Activity characterised in rat intestinal mucosa and liver; the modern molecular counterparts are glutaredoxins and TRP14, which reduce L-cystine with GSH.
rationale: A single thiol-disulfide exchange active site reduces cystine with two GSH; glutaredoxin's additional roles (deglutathionylation, iron-sulfur cluster delivery) are the same chemistry or non-catalytic, so it stays monofunctional.
direction_note: GSSG, the disulfide product that makes cystine reduction go, is absent from the ModelSEED equation (status MI:C:-20/H:-26/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2|CI:6), so the +435 kJ/mol GC estimate behind ModelSEED's reverse call is an artefact; with the GSH/GSSG pool held high in vivo the flux is always toward L-cysteine.

enzyme_name: Aryl (phenol) sulfotransferase, EC 2.8.2.1 - cytosolic SULT acting on the isoflavan equol
organism_context: Human liver/intestinal cytosolic sulfotransferases acting on the gut-microbial daidzein metabolite (S)-equol; equol-4'-sulfate and equol monosulfates are documented human plasma metabolites.
rationale: Cytosolic SULTs are single-domain PAPS-dependent transferases with one catalytic activity; no second catalytic function is reported for the SULT1/SULT2 families.
direction_note: PAPS is a high-energy sulfuryl donor and sulfonation is physiologically unidirectional; nothing in SULT enzymology supports regenerating PAPS from PAP plus an aryl sulfate, which is what ModelSEED's reverse call requires.

enzyme_name: Tetrachlorohydroquinone reductive dehalogenase PcpC (glutathione S-transferase family)
organism_context: Sphingobium (Sphingomonas/Flavobacterium) chlorophenolicum and Sphingomonas sp. UG30, pentachlorophenol degradation pathway.
rationale: PcpC is a single GST-fold polypeptide that runs successive reductive dehalogenations by the same glutathione-conjugate chemistry; repeated rounds on different chlorinated hydroquinones are substrate promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: The second GSH attacks the glutathionyl-hydroquinone conjugate to release the dechlorinated hydroquinone plus GSSG, but GSSG is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-20/H:-25/N:-6/O:-12/S:-2|CI:7), which is what produced the +416 kJ/mol estimate behind ModelSEED's reverse call.

enzyme_name: Tryptophanase (tryptophan indole-lyase, EC 4.1.99.1)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other enteric/anaerobic bacteria; MetaCyc assigns this half-reaction to TRYPDEG-PWY (L-tryptophan degradation II via pyruvate).
rationale: A single PLP active site performs beta-elimination; its activity on cysteine, serine and S-methylcysteine is substrate promiscuity at the same site, not a second catalytic activity. Called from established enzymology rather than a new search.
direction_note: Tryptophanase is reversible in vitro at high indole/pyruvate/NH3, but in the degradative pathway this entry belongs to the flux is L-Trp -> indole + 2-aminoacrylate, pulled on by hydrolysis of the aminoacrylate to pyruvate + NH3; the opposite (biosynthetic) use of this half-reaction belongs to tryptophan synthase, where the aminoacrylate never leaves the enzyme.

enzyme_name: Unassigned cyclisation step of the pvc (paerucumarin/pseudoverdine) pathway forming 2-isocyano-6,7-dihydroxycoumarin
organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa pvcABCD operon (PA2254-PA2257).
rationale: PvcA (isonitrile synthase, Rossmann fold) and PvcB (Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate oxygenase) are separate single-activity polypeptides acting upstream, and this particular ring-closure/tautomerisation of the isocyano-quinone to the coumarin is not assigned to a characterised protein and may be spontaneous.
direction_note: The pathway runs toward the coumarin (2-isocyano-6,7-dihydroxycoumarin is the pvc end product), so the acyclic isocyanopropenoate is the substrate and ring closure is the forward direction; ModelSEED's reverse call rests on a dGPredictor-only estimate with no group-contribution coverage.

enzyme_name: Unidentified ATP-dependent ascorbate kinase
rationale: No protein could be tied to this activity: PubMed returns zero records for 'ascorbate kinase' or 'ascorbic acid kinase' in title/abstract, and the known route to phosphorylated ascorbate is the PEP-dependent ascorbate PTS (UlaABC), not an ATP kinase.
direction_note: The phosphorylated ascorbate product is simply absent (status MI:C:-6/H:-6/O:-9/P:-1|CI:3), leaving ATP -> ADP as the only chemistry the estimator sees; any genuine ATP-dependent phosphorylation runs in the ATP-consuming direction, so ModelSEED's reverse call cannot be right.

enzyme_name: Kaempferol 3-O-glucoside 6''-O-feruloyltransferase, a BAHD-family hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA:flavonol-glucoside acyltransferase
organism_context: Plant flavonol acylglucoside biosynthesis (MetaCyc PWY-7168, Arabidopsis-type kaempferol derivatives); the specific gene is not pinned down by the literature searches.
rationale: BAHD acyltransferases are single-domain, single-active-site (HXXXD/DFGWG) acyl-CoA-dependent transferases with one catalytic activity; family-level assignment only, no specific protein identified.
direction_note: The feruloyl-CoA thioester is the activated donor, so acyl transfer onto the glucose 6''-OH is the downhill direction; running it backwards would mean synthesising a CoA thioester from an ordinary ester, which BAHD enzymes do not do without an energy input.

enzyme_name: Firefly luciferase (luciferin 4-monooxygenase, Luc) - adenylation half-reaction
organism_context: Photinus pyralis and other luminous beetles; beetle luciferases evolved from insect fatty acyl-CoA synthetases and extant luciferases often retain measurable ACS activity on one polypeptide.
rationale: One ANL-superfamily chain carries both the light-emitting luciferase activity and a genuine, retained fatty acyl-CoA synthetase activity (the ancestral function) - two distinct catalytic activities, not moonlighting. This entry is the L-luciferin branch, which luciferase adenylates and then thioesterifies to L-luciferyl-CoA rather than oxidising to light.
direction_note: Adenylation is the committed first half-reaction of both luciferase activities and is pulled forward by pyrophosphate hydrolysis; the reverse would require pyrophosphorolysis of luciferyl-adenylate, which is not the physiological flux. The bifunctionality is relevant here: it is the acyl-CoA-synthetase side of the enzyme that handles this (4R)/L-luciferin substrate.

enzyme_name: cis-p-Coumarate glucosyltransferase (UDP-glucose-dependent family-1 glycosyltransferase, EC 2.4.1.209)
organism_context: Plant UGT; no specific gene could be recovered - PubMed returns nothing for 'cis-p-coumarate' plus glucosyltransferase.
rationale: Family-1 UGTs are single-domain GT-B enzymes with one sugar-transfer activity; assignment here rests on the EC number rather than on an identified protein.
direction_note: The coumaroyl glucoside product (C15H17O8) is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-15/H:-17/O:-8|CI:1), so the direction call was made on ATP-like leftovers; UDP-glucose is the activated donor and glucosylation is the forward, downhill direction.

enzyme_name: Unidentified decarboxylative phenylcoumaran ring-opening enzyme converting (-)-DCA-CC to the stilbene DCA-S
organism_context: Sphingobium sp. SYK-6 (now S. lignivorans) dehydrodiconiferyl alcohol / beta-5 lignin dimer catabolism; Takahashi et al. demonstrated the decarboxylation and Calpha-Cbeta cleavage but identified no gene for this step, and the analogous ring opening in Novosphingobium aromaticivorans is done by a different enzyme (the gamma-formaldehyde lyase PcfL, which releases formaldehyde rather than CO2).
rationale: The catalysing protein is still unassigned in the SYK-6 pathway, so functionality cannot be judged; the closest characterised counterpart, PcfL, is a single-activity lyase.
direction_note: The catabolic flux releases CO2 and opens the ring to the stilbene, which lignostilbene dioxygenase then cleaves; a decarboxylation that loses CO2 to a downstream irreversible dioxygenase step cannot run backwards, so ModelSEED's reverse call is wrong despite eQuilibrator's +13.5 kJ/mol.

enzyme_name: Sirohydrochlorin cobaltochelatase CbiK / CbiX (class II chelatase, EC 4.99.1.3)
organism_context: Anaerobic cobalamin producers (Salmonella enterica CbiK; Bacillus megaterium and archaeal CbiX/CbiX-short), early-cobalt-insertion branch of adenosylcobalamin biosynthesis.
rationale: CbiK/CbiX insert Co(II) into sirohydrochlorin at a single active site; the long CbiX C-terminal histidine-rich region is a metal-binding extension, not a second catalytic activity (the genuinely multifunctional sibling, siroheme synthase CysG/Met8p, catalyses different reactions with Fe).
direction_note: Cobalt-sirohydrochlorin, the whole product, is missing (status MI:C:-42/Co:-1/H:-36/N:-4/O:-16|CI:8), leaving 'Co2+ + sirohydrochlorin -> 2 H+'; metal insertion into the tetrapyrrole is physiologically unidirectional, so the reverse call is an artefact.

enzyme_name: Inulosucrase (sucrose:2,1-beta-D-fructan 1-beta-D-fructosyltransferase, EC 2.4.1.9)
organism_context: Lactic acid bacteria (e.g. Lactobacillus johnsonii InuJ), glycoside hydrolase family GH68.
rationale: GH68 fructosyltransferases use one fructosyl-enzyme intermediate; transfer to a growing fructan versus to water (hydrolysis) is the same catalytic activity with a different acceptor, not a second function. Enzyme identified only from the EC number on the entry.
direction_note: Both the fructan acceptor and the extended fructan product are gone - the entry has collapsed to 'sucrose -> glucose' (status MI:C:-6/H:-10/O:-5). Sucrose is the activated donor, so glucose release is forward; glucose cannot be resynthesised into sucrose by this enzyme without the fructan.

enzyme_name: (-)-Medicocarpin (medicarpin 3-O-glucoside) beta-glucosidase, a plant GH1 glucosidase
organism_context: Medicago sativa / M. truncatula isoflavonoid phytoalexin conjugate turnover (MetaCyc PWY-2561); no specific gene recovered - searches on 'medicocarpin' and on Medicago isoflavone-conjugate glucosidases returned nothing usable.
rationale: GH1 beta-glucosidases are single-domain (beta/alpha)8 enzymes with one hydrolytic activity; the assignment here is from the chemistry (glucoside + H2O -> aglycone + glucose) rather than from an identified protein.
direction_note: Glucoside hydrolysis is strongly downhill and is how the phytoalexin is released from its storage conjugate; the opposite direction in planta goes through a UDP-glucose-dependent UGT, which is a different reaction, so free glucose + medicarpin -> medicocarpin (ModelSEED's call) has no enzyme behind it.

enzyme_name: Microsomal epoxide hydrolase (mEH, EPHX1)
organism_context: Mammalian liver endoplasmic reticulum; benzo[a]pyrene 4,5-oxide (the K-region epoxide) is a classical mEH substrate.
rationale: A single alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold catalytic site (Asp-His-Glu plus two tyrosines) opens the epoxide; mEH's reported role as a sodium-dependent bile-acid transporter is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional. Called from established enzymology.
direction_note: Hydrolytic opening of a strained arene oxide to the trans-dihydrodiol is irreversible; re-forming the epoxide from the diol is not something any hydrolase does, so ModelSEED's reverse call is unsupported (it rests on a dGPredictor-only estimate with no group-contribution coverage).

enzyme_name: Hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA:quinate hydroxycinnamoyltransferase (HQT/HCT, EC 2.3.1.133), BAHD family
organism_context: Plants - tomato, tobacco, sweet potato, coffee, globe artichoke; chlorogenic acid biosynthesis.
rationale: HQT/HCT are single-domain BAHD acyltransferases with one HXXXD-based acyl-transfer site; broad acceptor tolerance (quinate vs shikimate) is promiscuity, not bifunctionality.
direction_note: The p-coumaroylquinate ester product is missing (status MI:C:-16/H:-17/O:-8|CI:1), so there is nothing for the reaction to run back from. Worth flagging that this family genuinely does operate in reverse in planta (HCT regenerates caffeoyl-CoA from the shikimate ester in lignin biosynthesis), so a corrected, balanced version of this entry could reasonably be reversible rather than strictly forward.

enzyme_name: SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase of the nocamycin (ncm) post-tailoring set
organism_context: Saccharothrix syringae NRRL B-16468 nocamycin gene cluster; Mo et al. assign five enzymes (NcmEDGOP) to post-tailoring but do not say which one is the methyltransferase, so the specific protein is not pinned.
rationale: Class I SAM-dependent methyltransferases are single-Rossmann-domain, single-activity enzymes; assignment is at the family level only because the cluster paper does not resolve which ncm gene performs this methylation.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer is effectively irreversible (SAM is the high-energy donor and SAH is the spent product), so the biosynthetic direction nocamycin E -> BU-2313B is the only one with enzymology behind it.

enzyme_name: Hydration of dehydro(indol-3-yl)acetonitrile to the aryl cyanohydrin - likely non-enzymatic, within the FOX1-catalysed oxidation of indole-3-acetonitrile
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana 4-hydroxyindole-3-carbonyl nitrile (4-OH-ICN) pathogen-defence pathway, whose aryl cyanohydrin intermediate Rajniak et al. describe explicitly.
rationale: The step is a water addition across a highly electrophilic dehydro-nitrile and is most likely spontaneous rather than catalysed by a dedicated protein, so no enzyme can be assigned; the flanking two-electron oxidations are done by the FAD-dependent oxidase FOX1.
direction_note: ModelSEED is right here: the pathway runs indole-3-acetonitrile -> dehydro-nitrile -> aryl cyanohydrin -> indole-3-carbonyl nitrile, i.e. water adds to the dehydro species, and a cross-conjugated methide-type nitrile would in any case be quenched by water rather than regenerated from the alcohol. The LLM council's forward (dehydration) call inverts the biosynthetic flow; eQuilibrator (+10.4 kJ/mol for the dehydration) agrees with ModelSEED.

enzyme_name: Cystine C-S lyase (PLP-dependent beta-elimination by cystathionine beta/gamma-lyase-type enzymes, e.g. cystalysin, CTH/CSE)
organism_context: Treponema denticola cystalysin and mammalian cystathionine gamma-lyase both carry out cystine C-S lysis; the resulting 2-aminoacrylate is the reactive species Rid/RidA proteins quench.
rationale: One PLP active site performs the beta-elimination; the ability of these enzymes to act on cystathionine, cysteine and cystine is substrate promiscuity at the same site, and cystalysin's haemolytic behaviour is a downstream consequence of H2S production, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Beta-elimination from the PLP-cystine aldimine is pulled forward because the released 2-aminoacrylate tautomerises/hydrolyses on to pyruvate + ammonia; recondensing free thiocysteine with free aminoacrylate, which ModelSEED's reverse call implies, is not an enzymatic reaction.

enzyme_name: Type III pantothenate kinase (PanK-III / CoaX, EC 2.7.1.33)
organism_context: Bacteria lacking PanK-I/II (Helicobacter pylori, Bacillus anthracis, Thermotoga maritima and many pathogens).
rationale: PanK-III is a standalone ASKHA/acetate-kinase-fold phosphotransferase with one activity; the bifunctional enzyme of this pathway is the downstream CoaBC (phosphopantothenoylcysteine synthetase/decarboxylase), which is a different reaction. Called from established enzymology.
direction_note: 4'-Phosphopantothenate is absent (status MI:C:-9/H:-14/N:-1/O:-8/P:-1|CI:4), so the thermodynamic estimate is really for a bare ATP -> ADP conversion; a kinase runs in the ATP-consuming direction, so ModelSEED's reverse call is an artefact of the broken stoichiometry.

enzyme_name: Human carboxylesterase 1 (hCE1/CES1) - cocaine/ethanol transesterification to cocaethylene
organism_context: Human liver carboxylesterase 1; cocaethylene formation in co-users of cocaine and ethanol.
rationale: CES1 is a single alpha/beta-hydrolase-fold Ser-His-Glu esterase; hydrolysis and ethanol transesterification go through the same acyl-enzyme intermediate, so this is one catalytic activity with an alternative acyl acceptor, not bifunctionality.
direction_note: Methanol, the leaving alcohol, is missing (status MI:C:-1/H:-4/O:-1). The enzymology is transesterification of the cocaine methyl ester with ethanol, driven by the large ethanol excess in a drinking subject, so cocaethylene is the product, not the substrate.

enzyme_name: Ind3, a phenylacetate-CoA-ligase-like (ANL-superfamily) enzyme that drives indolmycin oxazolinone assembly; Ind6 acts as gatekeeper
organism_context: Streptomyces indolmycin producers; Du, Alkhalaf & Ryan reconstituted the pathway in vitro.
rationale: Ind3 is a single adenylating-domain ligase that condenses indolmycenic acid with dehydroarginine and drives the ring closure; Ind6's additional chaperone-like, outcome-directing role is explicitly not a second catalytic activity, and this ammonia-releasing cyclisation may itself be spontaneous once the amide is formed.
direction_note: Cyclisation with loss of ammonia is the committed, irreversible assembly of the oxazolinone ring; adding ammonia back onto indolmycin B to reopen the ring is not a reaction the pathway runs.

enzyme_name: Unassigned oxidative step of the fsr (8-O-methylfusarubin) pathway converting 8-O-methylanhydrofusarubinlactol to 8-O-methylfusarubinlactone
organism_context: Fusarium fujikuroi fsr naphthoquinone/fusarubin cluster (PKS fsr1, O-methyltransferase fsr2, monooxygenase fsr3); Studt et al. proposed the pathway from deletion phenotypes without assigning every tailoring step.
rationale: The specific fsr gene product for this step is not assigned in the literature, so functionality cannot be judged; the candidate (FSR3) is a single-activity FAD-dependent monooxygenase.
direction_note: ModelSEED is right here. The lactone (C16H14O8) carries one more oxygen than the anhydro-lactol (C16H14O7) at identical H count (status MI:O:-1), so the transformation is an oxygenation/oxidation of the lactol to the lactone; the redox partners (O2 plus NAD(P)H, or water plus NAD(P)+) have been stripped out. The LLM council's forward call would be a reductive deoxygenation of the lactone, which no enzyme in this cluster performs.

enzyme_name: Rid-family imine deaminase (Rid2/Rid3 subfamilies) hydrolysing 2-iminoarginine downstream of D-arginine dehydrogenase DauA; the hydrolysis also proceeds non-enzymatically
organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa D-arginine degradation (PWY-6422); Hodge-Hanson & Downs showed Rid2/Rid3 proteins, but not RidA/Rid1, deaminate iminoarginine generated in situ by DauA.
rationale: Rid proteins are small single-domain chorismate-mutase-fold deaminases with one catalytic activity; the same hydrolysis occurs slowly without protein, so enzymes here only accelerate a spontaneous step.
direction_note: Hydrolytic deamination of an imino acid to the 2-oxo acid plus ammonia is effectively irreversible and happens spontaneously in water, so the reverse direction ModelSEED recommends has no physical basis.

enzyme_name: Isoepoxydon synthase of the patulin (pat) cluster - gene not firmly assigned
organism_context: Penicillium expansum / Aspergillus clavatus patulin pathway (PWY-7490); the CYP619 P450s PatH and PatI are characterised for the earlier m-cresol and m-hydroxybenzyl alcohol hydroxylations, and PatN is the downstream isoepoxydon dehydrogenase, but no protein is firmly tied to isoepoxydon formation.
rationale: The catalysing protein for this step of the patulin pathway remains unassigned, so functionality is genuinely unknown rather than monofunctional by default.
direction_note: The entry is named for the product (isoepoxydon) and sits in a biosynthetic pathway whose next step, PatN, consumes isoepoxydon, so the forward (synthase) direction is correct. The equation balances only because MetaCyc uses H2O in place of the O2 plus reductant a dearomatising epoxidation actually requires, which is exactly what removes the irreversibility from the thermodynamic estimate.

enzyme_name: Tetraketide synthase / olivetol synthase (TKS, OLS), a type III polyketide synthase - derailment release of the tetraketide as its pyrone
organism_context: Cannabis sativa cannabinoid precursor pathway (MetaCyc PWY-7105); without its partner olivetolic acid cyclase (OAC, a separate DABB-fold polypeptide) TKS releases the linear tetraketide as the pyrone.
rationale: Type III PKSs run iterative condensation and cyclisation at one Cys-His-Asn active site on a single chain - one catalytic activity; OAC is a separate protein, so the TKS/OAC pair is a two-protein system, not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Lactonisation releases the CoA thioester and is irreversible - the free pyrone cannot re-acylate coenzyme A - so the only direction with enzymology behind it is tetraketide-CoA -> CoA + pyrone.
